newsitem.title: UK: British energy demand up 0.3 percent to end-Feb.
newsitem.headline: British energy demand up 0.3 percent to end-Feb.

text.p: British energy demand in the three months to the end of February rose 0.3 percent to 68.9 million tonnes of oil equivalent compared to the same period a year ago, the Department of Trade and Industry said on Tuesday.
Consumption of natural gas and and petroleum, including deliveries into storage, rose by 3.6 pct and 0.6 pct respectively while coal use fell by 10.8 percent.
Petroleum product consumption was 20.8 million tonnes, up 0.3 percent, with energy usage up 1.0 percent and non-energy usage down 2.4 percent.
Gasoline usage rose 1.5 percent on the year with unleaded deliveries rising to 69.9 percent of the total, up 3.6 percent.
Fuel oil deliveries fell by 4.6 percent.
